centralIdea.title: Assumptions vs Evidence and Insight.
centralIdea.paraA: There are a lot of assumptions about why customers buy, which work is most valuable, and where growth will come from. Some of them right. Some of them are focused on the business and not the customer. Some of them are old wives' tales. But one thing is for sure: assumptions are costing you money.
centralIdea.paraB: The Growth Program works to identify gaps and find the opportunities. It creates the environment where better decisions, stronger margins and clearer priorities come from.
centralIdea.quote: A stronger business isn't just about having more customers; it's about finding the right customers and focusing on the opportunities that will drive the growth you want. By understanding your business objectives, the value of your customers and where to focus your efforts, you build a stronger business — with clearer commercial choices and the ability to keep growing.
centralIdea.quoteAttribution: James Trebilcock, Founder, The United Republic

howItWorks.title: Five stages. One plan.
howItWorks.body: Each stage produces the evidence and decisions required for the next. We do not jump into action before we understand your business, your objectives, and what success looks like. A clear commercial direction is key to building lasting growth.

stages.title: The Business Now
stages.body: We find out how you and your team see the business today: your goals, customers, business model, capacity, risks and where you personally want to end up.

stages.title: The Opportunity
stages.body: We test assumptions against customer research, real numbers and market reality. Then we work out the value of each opportunity and prioritise the ones that will have the greatest effect.

stages.section: A clearer place in the market
stages.title: Branding & Positioning
stages.body: We work out what you're really selling, the problem you're solving for your customers, why the right customers should choose you, and how your business can stand apart in a way you can actually deliver on.

stages.section: Who matters and how to reach them
stages.title: Audiences, Messaging & Channel Planning
stages.body: We work out which customers matter most, who the decision-makers and influencers are, where the value is, shape the right messages for each audience, and find the best way to engage the influencers and decision-makers.

stages.title: Go To Market & Implementation
stages.body: We build a staged plan: who does what, when, what it costs, how you'll know it's working, and provide the tools your team needs to run it.

hero.title: From the real problem to work that performs.
hero.body: We work from problem definition through to delivery. Take one phase or the whole journey.

howWeWork.intro: Some organisations need help defining the problem. Some have a clear brief but need strategy and direction. Some need ongoing guidance to make sure execution stays true to the strategic intent.

phases.title: Diagnose
phases.tagline: We identify the problem behind the brief.
phases.body: Before any strategy work begins we need to understand what is really going on. Audience research, stakeholder insight, communications audits and strategic analysis — to define the real challenge rather than the symptoms.
phases.approach: Can run as a standalone diagnostic or as the foundation for everything that follows. The diagnostic output becomes the brief.

phases.title: Design
phases.tagline: We turn complexity into a clear plan.
phases.body: Once the problem is clear we build the strategy — the frameworks, plans and direction that guide decisions, shape creative development and keep activity aligned to outcomes.
phases.approach: Delivered as a complete plan, or built alongside your internal team to develop capability. Every strategy is designed to survive contact with reality.

phases.title: Direct
phases.tagline: We help the strategy survive contact with reality.
phases.body: Strategy only works if it is executed well. We help you identify and brief the right specialist partners, provide oversight during implementation, and keep the work true to the original intent.
delivers: Internal team support and capability building
phases.approach: This is where the tailored team model comes to life — creative, media, content producers and delivery teams, selected for the job rather than because they are already on the books.

phases.title: Measure
phases.tagline: We help you understand what worked and what to do next.
phases.body: Measuring outcomes is how we learn. Evaluate performance, test messages, review what worked, and plan refinements on evidence rather than instinct.
phases.approach: Evaluation feeds back into strategy, building a cycle of learning that makes future work sharper.

cta.title: Strategy through to delivery.
cta.body: We work from problem definition through to identifying, briefing and guiding the right execution partners.

hero.title: Start with the right questions. Then build the right response.
hero.paraA: Independent counsel for government, brands and complex organisations — before the money goes into campaigns, content or creative.
hero.paraB: We help you define the real problem, shape the strategy that answers it, and brief the right specialists to deliver it.

theCase.title: Most briefs describe a symptom.
theCase.paraA: By the time a brief reaches a supplier, the problem has usually been defined by whoever wrote it — and the response is shaped by whatever that supplier happens to sell.
theCase.paraB: We work upstream of that. What is the organisation actually trying to change? Who has to behave differently for it to happen? Where is influence genuinely available, and where is it being spent for no return?
theCase.paraC: Only then does it make sense to talk about what the work should be.

theDifference.title: Structurally independent.
theDifference.paraA: We don't keep a fixed team. We build the right people around each challenge — bringing together specialist partners for creative, media, content, production and delivery based on what the work needs, not what we happen to have in-house.
theDifference.paraB: No permanent team. No payroll to feed. No preferred answer waiting for a question.
theDifference.paraC: And we stay through delivery. Strategy that isn't carried into execution isn't strategy — it's a document.

steps.title: Understand
steps.body: Business objectives and success measures. Deep audience and stakeholder work. The true challenge rather than the presenting symptom — quantified, with segments, barriers and behaviours mapped.

steps.title: Strategise
steps.body: A customer-first roadmap, media-neutral from the outset. An Ideas Brief rather than a traditional creative brief. Built around message, medium and meaning — and the right idea, not the biggest one.

steps.title: Assemble and direct
steps.body: The specialist team built around the challenge, briefed properly and held to the strategy. Senior partners selected for fit. Lean, tailored, accountable to outcomes.

index.title: Case studies
index.paraA: Selected work across government, behaviour change, brand strategy and product launches — including some of Australia's largest brands and most complex stakeholder environments.
index.paraB: Every one of these started with a brief that described a symptom. The work was finding what was actually wrong.

items.title: Toyota — A Lifetime of Advantages
items.summary: Korean brands were winning on price. The research found Toyota was already winning the argument that actually mattered.

items.title: Ford — Six Model Launches in Six Months
items.summary: Six launches is not one problem six times. The work was sequencing and proportion, not six campaigns.

items.title: Commonwealth Bank — Little Card, Big Rewards
items.summary: Nobody wants a credit card. They want the thing it does — so that's what we said, in language people grasped immediately.

items.title: Snack Brands — Kettle Popcorn Launch
items.summary: A brand extension has to feel new enough to notice and familiar enough to still be Kettle. The task was knowing which parts to hold onto.

items.title: 2022 South Australian State Election
items.summary: Engaged to help procure an ad agency. Within weeks it was clear the communications function itself wasn't working.

items.title: 2022 Local Government Elections
items.summary: Postal voting isn't an awareness problem — it's a behaviour with more steps and more places to give up.

items.title: 2024 First Nations Voice to Parliament Election
items.summary: A new electoral process, six regions, and a timing change already working against understanding. Reach wasn't the constraint — trust was.

items.title: Adelaide Hills Wine Region
items.summary: The brief was positioning. The real obstacle was that members didn't agree on who the region was.

situation.heading: The situation
situation.body: Korean brands were competing hard on price and winning. Toyota was being pulled into a sticker-price argument it could not win without discounting its way down.

realProblem.heading: The real problem
realProblem.body: The brief was about price. The research said price was the wrong battleground entirely. A national programme with consumers and dealers found that people define value as the whole ownership experience — reliability, servicing, running costs, resale — not the number on the windscreen. Toyota was already winning that argument. It just was not having it.

whatWeDid.heading: What we did
items: Ran the national research programme with consumers and dealers

ford-six-model-launches.title: Ford — Six Model Launches in Six Months
ford-six-model-launches.attribution: National advertising and launch planning lead, [organisation], [years]

situation.heading: The situation
situation.body: Six vehicles to market in six months, in a slowing category, with new competitors arriving regularly and a dealer network that needed to stay confident.

realProblem.heading: The real problem
realProblem.body: Six launches is not one problem six times. Run separately they compete with each other for attention, budget and dealer energy — and the weakest one drags the rest down. The work was sequencing and proportion, not six campaigns.

whatWeDid.heading: What we did
items: Built national advertising and promotional plans across all six launches as one programme
Managed a $100m+ budget through a highly competitive market period
Targeted each launch to the right audience for the right reason rather than treating them alike
Strengthened position through Cricket Australia sponsorship and a major uplift in online presence

result.heading: The result
result.headline: FG Falcon became Ford's most successful launch since 2000.
result.body: Market share held above 13% through the period. All six launches delivered, with Ranger and FG Falcon carrying the programme.

whyItMatters.heading: Why it matters to you
whyItMatters.body: Most businesses have more they want to promote than attention to spend on it. Deciding what leads, what follows and what waits is worth more than doing all of it at once, badly.

cta.title: Got more you want to launch than attention to spend on it? That's a sequencing problem, not a budget one.
cta.body: Tell us what you're trying to grow — we'll come back to you within one business day.

commbank-little-card-big-rewards.title: Commonwealth Bank — Little Card, Big Rewards

situation.heading: The situation
situation.body: Launch CBA's first cash-back credit card into a crowded market. The brief was simple and almost impossible: make people care about another credit card.

realProblem.heading: The real problem
realProblem.body: Nobody wants a credit card. They want the thing the credit card does. Category language — rates, rewards, points, tiers — was making a genuinely simple benefit sound complicated, and complicated products do not get applied for.

whatWeDid.heading: What we did
items: Built a campaign that was clear, cheeky and plainly spoken
Explained cashback as money back, in language people grasped immediately
Deliberately avoided sounding like a bank
Made the value obvious from the first interaction rather than the fine print

result.heading: The result
result.headline: Online applications rose 30% after launch.
result.body: A national campaign built around one easily understood idea.

whyItMatters.heading: Why it matters to you
whyItMatters.body: If explaining what you sell takes more than a sentence, you are losing people before price is ever discussed. Clarity is not a creative flourish — it is a conversion mechanism.

cta.title: If your product needs more than a sentence to explain, that's the first thing worth fixing.
cta.body: Tell us what you're trying to grow — we'll come back to you within one business day.

situation.heading: The situation
situation.body: A brand extension into an already crowded popcorn category. It had to feel new enough to be worth noticing, and familiar enough to still be Kettle.

realProblem.heading: The real problem
realProblem.body: Brand extensions usually fail in one of two directions — too different and the equity does not transfer, too similar and there is no reason to buy. The real task was working out precisely which parts of Kettle were doing the work, and holding onto exactly those.

whatWeDid.heading: What we did
items: Developed the go-to-market plan for the launch
Built positioning and messaging around a premium tone with a slightly irreverent edge
Kept the proposition grounded in product truth rather than category cliché
Shaped execution so the product felt distinctive and recognisably Kettle

result.heading: The result
result.headline: The most successful brand extension launch in Snack Brands' history.
result.body: Ranging was secured in Coles, Woolworths, Metcash and independents.

whyItMatters.heading: Why it matters to you
whyItMatters.body: Adding a service or product line is the most common growth move a small business makes, and the most commonly botched. What you already have is worth more than the new thing — the trick is knowing which part.

state-election-2022.title: 2022 South Australian State Election
state-election-2022.attribution: Strategic lead, Electoral Commission of South Australia, [years]

situation.heading: The situation
situation.body: Three major electoral events approaching, participation declining, COVID pressures mounting and voter fatigue building after a federal election.

realProblem.heading: The real problem
realProblem.body: ECSA engaged us to help procure an advertising supplier. Within weeks it was clear that was not the problem. The communications function itself was not working — no strategic framework, no crisis capability, and no way for a new supplier to succeed even if one were appointed. They did not need a better supplier. They needed a function that could brief one.

whatWeDid.heading: What we did
items: Delivered a full capability review and identified the structural gaps
Built a multi-year strategy aligned to operational realities and government obligations
Established a crisis communications framework from scratch
Ran statewide research to identify audience segments, behavioural barriers and channel needs
Directed strategy, creative, media, PR and crisis communications through to implementation

result.heading: The result
result.headline: 92% participation maintained through COVID conditions and voter fatigue.
result.body: Targeted engagement reached CALD communities, young people and disengaged voters.

whyItMatters.heading: Why it matters to you
whyItMatters.body: The thing you have decided to buy is frequently not the thing you need. That is worth knowing before you spend the money, not after.

local-government-elections-2022.title: 2022 Local Government Elections
local-government-elections-2022.attribution: Campaign strategy lead, Electoral Commission of South Australia, 2022

situation.heading: The situation
situation.body: Council elections are voluntary and had been stuck near 30% participation for years, with some districts below 15%. They also fell in the same calendar year as two major parliamentary elections.

realProblem.heading: The real problem
realProblem.body: This was not an awareness problem. Postal voting asks people to complete and return a ballot themselves — a different behaviour with more steps and more places to give up. Telling more people about the election would not have moved it.

whatWeDid.heading: What we did
items: Built an integrated campaign across enrolment, nominations and voting rather than one message
Built awareness of timing and responsibilities, not just the event
Encouraged business enrolment and promoted early completion and return of ballots
Co-ordinated messaging across ECSA, councils and the LGA

result.heading: The result
result.headline: Participation lifted from 30% to over 34% — more than 10% growth against a long-term decline.
result.body: First-week postal ballot returns rose 300%, which improved processing efficiency and delivered results faster.

whyItMatters.heading: Why it matters to you
whyItMatters.body: Getting someone to act is a different job from getting them to notice. Most marketing that fails has done the first and skipped the second.

cta.title: Getting people to notice and getting them to act are two different jobs. Let's talk about which one you're missing.

situation.heading: The situation
situation.body: One of Australia's leading cool climate wine regions, widely respected, and without a clear story about itself.

realProblem.heading: The real problem
realProblem.body: The brief was brand positioning. The actual obstacle was internal: members did not agree on who the region was, who it competed against, or what it should say to consumers, visitors, government, industry bodies and sponsors. No amount of positioning work survives that. Agreement had to come first.

whatWeDid.heading: What we did
items: Ran an extensive qualitative and quantitative research programme across consumers, stakeholders, industry and government
Clarified who the region was, what it stood for, where it was heading and why anyone should believe it
Defined how the region should talk about itself in a way that united members rather than dividing them
Built the brand positioning, architecture and communications strategy from the research

result.heading: The result
result.headline: A research-led positioning and a clearer regional narrative.
result.body: Giving members a shared platform for visitation, partnerships, government engagement and events.

first-nations-voice-2024.title: 2024 First Nations Voice to Parliament Election
first-nations-voice-2024.attribution: Communications strategy lead, Electoral Commission of South Australia, 2023–24

situation.heading: The situation
situation.body: South Australia's first First Nations Voice election — 46 positions across six regions, held on 16 March 2024. Originally scheduled for September 2023 and moved to avoid overlapping the Federal Voice Referendum.

realProblem.heading: The real problem
realProblem.body: Standard election advertising was never going to carry this. A new electoral process, communities spread across six regions, and a timing change that had already disrupted understanding. Reach was not the constraint — trust and comprehension were.

whatWeDid.heading: What we did
items: Identified early that conventional advertising alone would not work, and built a community-led approach instead
Combined communications strategy, community engagement, media engagement, advertising, PR and budget management
Delivered across TV, press, outdoor, digital, website, social and PR
Created more than 500 community engagement kits and supported over 400 engagement sessions

result.heading: The result
result.headline: All 46 positions attracted multiple nominations.
result.body: Not one was filled uncontested, and elections were successfully held across every position — establishing the First Nations Voice to SA Parliament.

whyItMatters.heading: Why it matters to you
whyItMatters.body: When the people you need are not reachable through the obvious channels, spending more on those channels does not fix it. Going where they already are does.

cta.title: When the obvious channels aren't reaching the people you need, that's a strategy problem before it's a media-buying one.
